Theme

Latin word

hospes

hospes, hospitis m./f.

noun, third declension; feminine hospita, hospitae

guest (staying in the house); also host; host (and also guest); guest, visitor

In this lexicon

  • guest

    also used · classical · Traupman 324

  • host

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. S. 1.5.71: sēdulus hospes; Cic. Div. 1.57: alterum ad caupōnem dēvertisse, ad hospitem alterum (Lewis & Short)

  • visitor

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 64.1: hospitēs vēnisse; Ov. F. 5.502: hospitibus jānua nostra patet; Traupman 402

  • hospes āërius: steward

    modern

Examples

  • sēdulus hospes paene macrōs ārsit dum turdōs versat in ignī

    our attentive host nearly burnt down while turning lean thrushes over the fireHor. S. 1.5.71–72

    In the entry for host

  • cum dēfēcēre, quī modo hospes fuerat, mōnstrātor hospitiī et comes

    when the food has run out, the man who was host a moment ago becomes guide to another welcome, and companionTac. Germ. 21.2–3

    In the entry for host

  • hic est leō hospes hominis, hic est homō medicus leōnis

    this is the lion who was the man’s host, this is the man who was the lion’s doctorGell. 5.14.30

    In the entry for host

  • sī vespertīnus subitō tē oppresserit hospes

    if a visitor descends on you suddenly in the eveningHor. S. 2.4.17

    In the entry for visitor

  • et hospitibus jānua nostra patet

    and our door is open to visitorsOv. F. 5.502

    In the entry for visitor

    guest, you will be well off staying here; here the highest good is pleasureSen. Ep. 21.10
